messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty P1 fired — gpu-node-72 (us-west-2 / rack-9). Symptom: kernel panic + kubelet NotReady. Auto-escalation to on-call (pagerduty).

pagerduty: PagerDuty event: INC-219876. Trigger rule: node-kernel-panic-detection. Priority: P1. Primary: @alex (ack required).

alex: acked and taking lead. attaching serial console now. moving to the node stdout to check oops.

ops-runner: pulled logs from node (nvme + driver messages). snippet: ```
[  123.456789] Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception in interrupt
[  123.456792] RIP: 0010:0xffffffff810d2abc
[  123.456795] Code: Bad RIP value 0x0
```

marta: if kernel panic confirmed we should cordon and drain the node then failover replicas. is this hitting model-serving pods?

alex: yes, 3 replicas of embedding-worker-2 were on that host. The router already rerouted some requests but we're seeing increased queue times on embedding-api in us-west-2. No customer-facing 5xxs in last 2m, but tail latency up ~200-400ms for embeddings.

nina: starting evacuation: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-72 && kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data gpu-node-72` — running now.

ops-runner: drain output: ```
Warning: ignoring DaemonSet-managed pods: kube-proxy, node-exporter
evicting pod embedding-worker-2-rlv9 (grace period 30s)
pod embedding-worker-2-rlv9 deleted
All pods on gpu-node-72 removed.
```

alex: good. also triggered auto-routing fallback to cheapest-compatible model-variant in us-west-1 for heavy embedding traffic (policy: latency-tier-fallback). That should reduce client impact.

marta: we've created INC-219876 in the tracker and linked this thread. Severity: P1 (potential customer impact). Notifying CS to prep for customer messages. @sre-oncall you good to take next shift if this goes long?

sre-oncall: can take handoff in 30m. please include steps done and any followups.

ops-runner: node is currently unreachable for SSH (serial attached but stopped at oops). I've scheduled a reboot via BMC next. submitting reboot job now.

alex: quick checklist for handoff: 1) node cordoned + drained (done), 2) router fallback active (done), 3) ticket INC-219876 created (link: https://tracker.redwoodinc/INC-219876), 4) BMC reboot scheduled, 5) no client 5xxs observed but higher latency for embeddings in US-WEST, 6) postmortem owner: marta.

marta: adding runbook reference: https://runbooks.redwoodinc/ops/node-kernel-panic — followed steps A-C so far. next: if reboot fails we move to decommission and reprovision.

nina: BMC reboot kicked, waiting for power cycle. serial shows ACPI handoff and then board POST.

incident-bot: Automated monitoring note: autoscaler observed increased queue length on embeddings-batch and spun up 2 extra preemptible workers in us-west-1. Cost impact minimal due to preemptible pool.

alex: talking to CS: flagged two customers using bulk-embed jobs — reached out to explain potential delays and that we routed to fallback region. CS ticket numbers: CS-7881, CS-7882.

ops-runner: node came back to POST but kernel oops persists on boot. current console: ```
[   45.123456] Kernel panic - not syncing: Unable to handle kernel paging request at virtual address 0xdeadbeef
[   45.123459] Rebooting in 1 seconds...
```

marta: ok looks like HW or driver-level issue. mark node for deprovision and reprovision host. Alex, can you handoff? I'll own post-incident writeup.

alex: handing off to @sre-oncall now — I'm stepping out. summary in INC-219876 comment. :handshake:

sre-oncall: ack, taking over. actions for next 8h: reprovision gpu-node-72, run driver validation on new host, check NVMe SMART, run warmup load test for model-serving. will update ticket and this thread.

nina: adding note: cluster autoscaler will unblock resources in ~10m as new nodes spin up. monitor embedding latency dashboards (link: https://dashboards.redwoodinc/embeddings/latency).

marta: final note for postmortem: affected workload = embeddings batch + a few realtime embedding replicas; root cause suspected = kernel panic due to driver/hw mismatch; mitigations = cordon/drain + fallback routing + reboot attempt + reprovision. Postmortem owner: marta.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: incident acknowledged and escalated per policy. Next escalation will notify infra-leads if no resolution in 2 hours.

alex: thanks everyone. closing live ops — moving to post-incident workspace.
